BackDown 1.0.0-beta.6

The sixth beta of BackDown 1.0: tags that follow a file's content across every copy of it, a photo's date and place read from the photo itself and turned into country, region, city and nearest airport without going online, and scans that refuse to run against the wrong drive.

  • Tags, flags and links

  • Under the hood

Released 2026-11-07 · downloads and checksums on GitHub · Download page The sixth beta of BackDown 1.0: tags that follow a file's content across every copy of it, a photo's date and place read from the photo itself and turned into country, region, city and nearest airport without going online, and scans that refuse to run against the wrong drive.

Install#

PlatformInstallerCommand line
Linux x86-64backdown-io_1.0.0-beta.6_amd64.deb (Debian, Ubuntu) or .AppImagebackdown-v1.0.0-beta.6-linux-x86_64.tar.gz (static)
Linux ARM64backdown-io_1.0.0-beta.6_arm64.deb or .AppImagebackdown-v1.0.0-beta.6-linux-arm64.tar.gz (static)
macOS (Apple silicon + Intel)BackDown-1.0.0-beta.6.dmgbackdown-v1.0.0-beta.6-macos-universal.tar.gz
Windows x86-64BackDown-1.0.0-beta.6-x64.msi (no administrator rights needed)backdown-v1.0.0-beta.6-windows-x86_64.zip

This release is signed. SHA256SUMS.txt.sig is an Ed25519 signature of SHA256SUMS.txt by BackDown's release key, and backdown update checks it before installing anything. To check by hand, see Air-gapped computers.

The installers and apps themselves still aren't signed by Apple or Microsoft. On macOS, right-click the app and choose Open the first time (for the command-line binary: xattr -d com.apple.quarantine backdown). On Windows, SmartScreen may ask you to confirm once.

What's new since beta.5#

Tags, flags and links#

  • Tags say what something is about: its owner, kind, place, country, city, airport, event, date. backdown tag add --kind city --value "Hong Kong" --to TARGET, tag rm, tag list, tag of TARGET. Tags can nest (a city under its country).
  • A tag on a file's content (content:<sha256>) is on every copy of that file, on any drive, and stays when copies are moved or deduplicated. Tags can also go on a person or database (subject:, entity:) or a path (path:).
  • Flags record decisions: canonical, duplicate (of which copy), keep, drop, reviewed, mine, not-mine and others. backdown flag set|clear|of.
  • Links between any two things: backdown edge add SRC REL DST, edge from, edge to.
  • --json on everything that reads. Each tag and flag remembers where it came from and when.

A photo's date and place#

  • backdown tag exif FILES reads the date and GPS position a photo or video recorded (JPEG, HEIC, TIFF, MOV, MP4) and tags its content with the year, the date under it, and the location. The files need to be indexed; one BackDown hasn't hashed yet (a file no other file matches in size never is) is hashed there and then.
  • backdown tag geo turns those locations into country, region, city and nearest airport (within 120 km), offline, from place data built into BackDown. Nothing is sent anywhere. The further a photo is from the nearest town, the lower the confidence recorded with the tag.
  • backdown tag geo --about shows the data it uses and where it comes from: GeoNames (CC BY 4.0) and OurAirports (public domain).

Scans refuse the wrong drive#

After a reboot on a user's server, a drive came up at a different mount point, and other software had already made a few folders at its usual one. BackDown's next scan saw those folders instead of the drive and marked almost 16 million files as gone; getting them back would have meant hashing terabytes again. Scans now stop before recording anything when:

  • another drive is where the scanned one was: the folder is now on a different disk (by serial or file system UUID) from the last scan. The message names both and says what to do: mount the drive there, or backdown index --allow-other-drive for a new drive in the old one's place, or backdown forget and index it afresh.
  • no files are found where the last scan found some (--allow-empty overrides, as before);
  • the folder itself can't be read, even with --allow-empty.

A folder lower down that can't be read keeps its files as they were, rather than counting them as deleted. A refused scan leaves no trace in the history.

Under the hood#

  • The licence list shipped with every download covers the new components, and credits the place data.

Known limitations#

  • Built locally, not by CI. Every test passed on Linux; the macOS and Windows builds are checked but haven't yet run on those systems. Please report anything that doesn't work: https://github.com/BuenGenio/backdown-releases/issues
  • Tags, flags and links are command-line only for now; the browser and the app don't show them yet.
  • tag exif and tag geo run when you ask, not after each scan.
  • Places are matched to the nearest town of 1,000 people or more, so a photo taken in remote country gets the nearest such town.
  • The installers aren't signed or notarised by Apple or Microsoft.
  • Pro, Team and Forensic features are free during the beta; pricing may change before 1.0.
  • A machine running Windows can't be the other end of backdown remote yet.

Documentation: https://backdown.io/docs/. Provided as-is, without warranty, for evaluation.
